symptom: In a project with layout-config.yaml every flow mxcli wrote gained an `@mxcli-layout: …` line in its Documentation — Studio Pro's documentation pane, generated docs and DESCRIBE output — even when the style was the project's; leaving it out of the doc comment did not remove it, because the write appended it again.
cause: The style a flow was drawn in was recorded per flow in user content so DESCRIBE could judge positions against it after the project changed style.
fix: The marker is never written. DESCRIBE reads an unmarked flow in the project style (the one create or modify rebuilds in), so derived positions are judged against what exec will do; a flow drawn in another style prints the @position lines that keep it. A legacy marker is honoured once and removed by the next write or `layout flows`.
insight: Inferring the style from geometry (try project, then default) sounds free but breaks the round trip: exec has nothing to tell it the description was derived against the default, so it rebuilds in the project style. The only style DESCRIBE may treat as derivable is the one exec will use. The guard shape (flowLooksLikeGuardContinuation) had to read the project style too, or guard flows printed positions.
test: flowlayout_config_test.go TestWithoutFlowLayoutMarker, TestResolveFlowLayout; flowlayout_describe_test.go TestDescribeJudgesPositionsAgainstTheProjectStyle (control: project back on default prints positions). Reverting the describe fallback fails the guard case; re-adding the stamp fails 'wrote a marker'. Live 11.17.0 on the issue's repro: no line in bson, no @position, second exec unchanged; legacy marker stripped, round trip unchanged; mx check 0 errors.
